title: bug: moe-proxy reads .moe/daemon.json with no size cap
description:
Objective: bound packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts readDaemonInfoResult. It calls fs.readFileSync on the whole .moe/daemon.json on every connect and reconnect. Wrapper RPCs and heartbeats spawn a fresh proxy for every call, so an oversize file is read again on each call. This is a sibling of task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e (the JetBrains reader, 64 KiB cap). daemon.json is repository content, and a huge or never-ending file (a symlink to /dev/zero) exhausts memory.

Deliverable:
- A bounded read of at most 65537 bytes: fs.openSync plus fs.readSync into a 65537-byte Buffer, with the descriptor closed in finally.
- A larger file returns { info: null, retryable: false, error: 'daemon.json is larger than 64 KiB' }, so the proxy exits with that JSON-RPC error through the existing non-retryable path.
- A missing file stays retryable, a malformed file keeps its current error, and valid files behave as today.

Not in scope: index.ts reconnect logic, the README, and the other clients, which have their own sibling tasks.

Depends on task-eb85340bf5ee4bde84ca8658a0ca0cd2, which also edits utils.ts.

Verification: cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test. Never run it in the shared checkout: live WSL seats run that checkout's gitignored dist through the global moe-proxy symlink, and pretest's clean deletes dist first. Run it from a git-archive snapshot with a native npm ci (Serena mem gotcha-proxy-npm-test-shared-checkout-deletes-dist).
definitionOfDone: readDaemonInfoResult parses a valid 65536-byte daemon.json, and for a 65537-byte file returns { info: null, retryable: false, error: 'daemon.json is larger than 64 KiB' }, proven by new utils.test.ts cases.
The read never takes more than 65537 bytes and closes its descriptor on every path, proven by a test (for example, a sparse multi-GiB file is refused promptly).
A missing daemon.json stays retryable and a malformed one keeps its existing error, proven by the existing readDaemonInfo tests passing unchanged.
Fresh cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test exits 0, run from an isolated snapshot, never in the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
RED first (load test-driven-development). The cap contract is shared with JetBrains task-4f1e37f3 and the daemon row task-91ef7886: 64 KiB is 65536 bytes; read at most 65537 bytes through one descriptor; a larger file is refused like invalid connection details and never deleted. The tests pin 65536 and 65537 as literals. Pad JSON.stringify(info) with trailing spaces to an exact byte length. Before editing, confirm prerequisite task-eb85340b landed (its injectWorkerType sits elsewhere in utils.ts) and work on top of it. NEVER run npm test, npm run build/clean or tsc in the shared checkout's packages/moe-proxy: live WSL seats run its gitignored dist through the global moe-proxy symlink. All runs happen in the step 3 snapshot.

packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.test.ts, in describe('readDaemonInfo'):
(1) A valid 65536-byte daemon.json gives readDaemonInfo toEqual(info). The 65537-byte version gives readDaemonInfoResult toEqual({ info: null, retryable: false, error: 'daemon.json is larger than 64 KiB' }).
(2) Bounded read. Spy (pass-through) on fs.readFileSync, fs.readSync and fs.closeSync; utils.ts imports fs as a default import, so the spies see its calls. For an 8 MiB daemon.json: the oversize result above is returned, readFileSync is never called with the daemon.json path, the readSync return values sum to at most 65537, and closeSync runs once.
(3) POSIX only (it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')): a daemon.json that is a symlink to /dev/zero gives the same oversize result promptly. Metadata reports size 0, so only the bounded read stops it.
(4) The existing missing-file (retryable), malformed-JSON, malformed-port and project-mismatch cases stay unchanged and green.

packages/moe-proxy/src/index.test.ts: next to the existing 'returns clear JSON-RPC error for daemon.json project mismatch' test, and copying its spawn and cleanup pattern:
(5) A proxy spawned at a testDir whose daemon.json is 65537 bytes of valid JSON exits with code 1, and its first stdout line's error.message is 'daemon.json is larger than 64 KiB'.

In the snapshot, (1)'s oversize case, (2), (3) on POSIX and (5) fail on today's code. Record that.

amendments.description:
RED first (load test-driven-development).

The cap contract is shared with JetBrains task-4f1e37f3 and the daemon row task-91ef7886:
- 64 KiB is 65536 bytes;
- read at most 65537 bytes through one descriptor;
- a larger file is refused like invalid connection details and never deleted.

The tests pin 65536 and 65537 as literals. Pad JSON.stringify(info) with trailing spaces to an exact byte length.

Before editing, confirm prerequisite task-eb85340b landed (its injectWorkerType sits elsewhere in utils.ts) and work on top of it.

NEVER run npm test, npm run build/clean or tsc in the shared checkout's packages/moe-proxy: live WSL seats run its gitignored dist through the global moe-proxy symlink. All runs happen in the step 3 snapshot.

SAFETY: do NOT add a /dev/zero case, or any other never-ending device, and never point a test at one.
- Today's whole-file readFileSync of /dev/zero never reaches EOF. It grows memory until the process dies, and a synchronous read cannot be stopped by the vitest timeout.
- On the daemon row task-91ef7886, exactly that RED run got its vitest worker killed with SIGTERM.
- Case (2)'s exact read total proves the bound without one.

packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.test.ts, in describe('readDaemonInfo'):

(1) A valid 65536-byte daemon.json gives readDaemonInfo toEqual(info). The 65537-byte version gives readDaemonInfoResult toEqual({ info: null, retryable: false, error: 'daemon.json is larger than 64 KiB' }).

(2) Bounded read. Spy, pass-through, on fs.readFileSync, fs.openSync, fs.readSync and fs.closeSync. utils.ts and the test both import fs from 'fs', so the spies see its calls. Write an 8 MiB daemon.json: valid JSON padded with spaces. Assert:
- the oversize result above is returned;
- readFileSync is never called with the daemon.json path;
- openSync opened the daemon.json path exactly once;
- the readSync return values for that descriptor sum to exactly 65537. Exact, not "at most": a size pre-check that never reads gives 0, and an unbounded read gives more;
- closeSync received that descriptor exactly once.

(3) Error path. Mock fs.readSync to throw an Error whose code is 'EIO', for a valid small daemon.json. Assert:
- readDaemonInfoResult returns the existing invalid-details result unchanged: { info: null, retryable: false, error: 'daemon.json contains invalid daemon connection details' };
- closeSync still received the descriptor openSync returned.

Restore every spy in afterEach (vi.restoreAllMocks()), so a failing assertion cannot leak a mock into later cases.

(4) The existing missing-file (retryable), malformed-JSON, malformed-port and project-mismatch cases stay unchanged and green.

packages/moe-proxy/src/index.test.ts, next to the existing 'returns clear JSON-RPC error for daemon.json project mismatch' test, copying its spawn pattern and its 5-second kill timeout:

(5) A proxy spawned at a testDir whose daemon.json is 65537 bytes of valid JSON for this project exits with code 1. Its first stdout line's error.message is 'daemon.json is larger than 64 KiB'.

In the snapshot, (1)'s oversize case, (2), (3) and (5) fail on today's code. (5) fails by the copied 5-second kill timeout, which also reaps the child. Record that.
amendments.reason: Removes the /dev/zero case. Against today's unbounded read it never reaches EOF and grows memory until the process dies; the daemon row task-91ef7886's RED vitest worker was killed with SIGTERM that way. An exact read-total assertion and a forced-IO-error case prove the bound and the descriptor close instead.

implementationPlan.description:
Verification gate, run once: cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test, from an isolated snapshot. The shared checkout's dist is what live WSL seats run, and pretest's clean deletes it first (mem:gotcha-proxy-npm-test-shared-checkout-deletes-dist).
- ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); SNAP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-685d-gate.XXXXXX).
- git -C $ROOT archive HEAD packages/moe-proxy | tar -x -C $SNAP.
- Check that package.json, package-lock.json and tsconfig.json equal HEAD.
- Overlay exactly the three owned files and cmp each one.
- (cd $SNAP/packages/moe-proxy && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund) with the Linux node/npm.
- From $SNAP run (cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test) in the seat's normal environment; vitest.config blanks the seat's MOE_* exports.

Require exit 0 and zero failed tests. Confirm the shared checkout's packages/moe-proxy/dist/index.js stat is unchanged. complete_task gets { command: '(cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test)', exitCode, outputTail }, plus the tested root and base commit. If npm ci cannot reach the registry, report_blocked with the error; never fall back to an in-place run. Error handling: on a failure, fix the cause, re-overlay and re-run; never weaken an assertion.

reopenReason: Human asked the architect seat to promote and plan the daemon.json size-cap follow-ups (2026-10-27).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) An fs.statSync size pre-check: rejected. Device symlinks report size 0, so the read itself must be bounded, as in the JetBrains and daemon rows. (2) Treating oversize as retryable: rejected. Every invalid daemon.json is non-retryable today, and an oversize file is not a daemon's; the proxy exits with a clear message instead of re-reading a huge file every reconnect. (3) A shared helper package: rejected. The packages have no workspaces, so each keeps a tiny private bounded read. (4) A sparse multi-GiB file test: rejected. Node zero-fills on NTFS, which is slow on Windows CI. An 8 MiB file plus fs spies proves the bound on every OS, and /dev/zero covers lying metadata on POSIX.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- utils.ts:83 readDaemonInfoResult. It returns a retryable result when the file is missing. Shape and project mismatches, and any read or parse error caught by its catch, are non-retryable with a fixed error string.
- index.ts:366 connect() turns a non-retryable error into writeError plus process.exit(1).
- index.test.ts:42 already spawns the built proxy against a mismatched daemon.json and asserts exit 1 plus the error message. Copy that pattern.
- utils.test.ts describe('readDaemonInfo') at :25 holds the existing cases.
- utils.ts imports fs as a default import, so vi.spyOn(fs, ...) intercepts its calls.
- Prerequisite task-eb85340b adds injectWorkerType to utils.ts, in a different region.
planningNotes.risks: Shared dist hazard: never run npm test, build or clean in the shared checkout's packages/moe-proxy. The global moe-proxy symlinks to it and live WSL seats run its dist; the shared node_modules is a Windows install. utils.ts is also edited by task-eb85340b, and dependsOn serializes this row behind it. Test (3) is skipped on Windows by design. The cap is a cross-package contract: do not change 64 KiB here.
